cards.text: The psalmist is still talking to the LORD, and this part opens with something personal: God's own hands made him and fashioned him. The Millers carved my name into my handle ONE time, and I still bring it up at parties. This man got shaped by the hands of God Himself!

cards.question: So the psalmist turns to the One who made him. What does he ask his Maker to give him?

answers.text: Strength to defeat all his enemies
Riches to take care of his family

cards.text: Then he tells the LORD he wants the people who fear Him to see him and rejoice. When I walk into a room, the only thing that lights up is the oven, and that's because I turned it ON.

cards.question: The psalmist says people who fear God can rejoice when they see him, because he has hoped in God's ___.

cards.text: Then he says he knows the LORD's judgments are righteous. And he says something about his own hard times, too.

cards.question: The psalmist says the LORD afflicted him in faithfulness.

cards.text: Now the requests start coming. First, he asks for the LORD's loving devotion to comfort him, according to His promise to His servant.

cards.question: Next, the psalmist asks for the LORD's compassion to come to him. What does he want it to do for him?
In that same breath, the psalmist calls God's law his ___.

cards.text: Then the arrogant are back, subverting him with a lie, and he asks that they be put to shame. Somebody spreads a lie about ME, I'm in the group chat typing in ALL CAPS for an hour.

cards.question: With the arrogant lying about him, what does the psalmist say he will do?
The psalmist asks that people who know God's testimonies would turn away from him.

cards.text: The last line of this stretch is about his own heart. He asks that it be blameless in God's statutes.

cards.question: Why does the psalmist want his heart to be blameless in God's statutes?

answers.text: So he won't be put to shame
So kings will give him honor
So he'll grow rich in old age

cards.text: The next stretch starts heavy: his soul faints for God's salvation, and he's waiting for God's word. Waiting, friend. Like staring at those three dots in a text that NEVER turn into a message.

cards.question: The psalmist's eyes fail from looking for God's promise. What does he ask the LORD while he waits?

answers.text: Why did You ever make me
Where have You gone to now

cards.text: Then he says he's like a wineskin dried up by smoke. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, so I know that look.

cards.question: Dried up like a wineskin in the smoke, the psalmist says he has forgotten God's statutes.
Still waiting, the psalmist asks the LORD how many days His servant must wait. What else does he want to know?

answers.text: When God will judge his persecutors
Why his closest friends have left him
Where his family has been taken to

cards.text: That lie from earlier? That was the warm-up. Now the arrogant have dug pits for him, in violation of God's law.
He tells the LORD all His commandments are faithful. Then he cries out for help.

cards.question: Why does the psalmist say he is being persecuted?

answers.text: There's no cause for it at all
He broke one of the king's laws
He stole land from his neighbor

cards.text: They almost wiped him from the earth, and friend, that word ALMOST is carrying this whole verse.

cards.question: Even after nearly being wiped from the earth, the psalmist says he has not forsaken God's precepts.
He ends this stretch asking the LORD to ___ him according to His loving devotion, so he can ___ the testimony of God's mouth.

cards.text: After all that waiting, the pits and the smoke, the psalmist turns from his troubles to the LORD's word.

cards.question: What does the psalmist say about the LORD's word?

answers.text: It is everlasting and fixed in the heavens
It is hidden and hard for anyone to find
It is only for the priests in the temple

cards.text: He says the LORD's faithfulness continues through all generations. My oven timer can't even make it through ONE batch without me checking on it.

cards.question: The psalmist says the LORD established the earth, but it won't last.

cards.text: Then he says God's ordinances stand to this day.

cards.question: Why does the psalmist say God's ordinances still stand?

answers.text: Because all things are His servants
Because the priests stand guard over them
Because the kings make the people obey

cards.question: The psalmist looks back on his hard times. If God's law hadn't been his delight, what does he say would have happened?

answers.text: He would have perished in his affliction
He would have become a powerful king
He would have sailed far away to sea

cards.question: The psalmist says he will never forget God's precepts, because by them God has ___ him.

cards.text: Then he says it plain: "I am Yours; save me, for I have sought Your precepts." If I'd known that line back in the junk drawer, I'd have YELLED it every time the light came in.

cards.question: The wicked are waiting to destroy the psalmist. What does he say he'll do?

answers.text: Ask the king to step in

cards.text: Last line of this stretch: he says he has seen a limit to all perfection. Ask me about it, friend, my edges went soft YEARS ago.

cards.question: The psalmist says God's commandment has a limit too.

cards.text: And that's where we'll set this one on the cooling rack. Don't go anywhere, friend, this psalm still has more to say.

findings.problem: Verse 74 is a wish: 'May those who fear You see me and rejoice.' The question turns it into a plain statement that they 'can rejoice when they see him.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card says 'Now the requests start coming. First, he asks...' at verse 76. But he already made requests in verse 73 ('give me understanding') and verse 74 ('May those who fear You see me'), and card 2 already asked what he requested. What the card points out isn't true.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: 'Then the arrogant are back' says the arrogant appeared before. Nothing earlier in this passage sets that up. It leans on earlier verses (like Ps 119:69) that the card doesn't cite. The card cites only Psalm 119:78.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The joke compares waiting on God to waiting on a text whose 'three dots... NEVER turn into a message.' That casts God as the one who never answers, so the humor aims at God.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: This isn't the passage's opening card, but it has three sentences: 'The next stretch starts heavy...', 'Waiting, friend.' and 'Like staring at...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This isn't the passage's opening card, but it has three sentences: 'That lie from earlier?', 'That was the warm-up.' and 'Now the arrogant have dug pits...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card retells details from verses 81 to 85 ('all that waiting, the pits and the smoke') but cites only Psalm 119:89. Its citation is narrower than what it uses. It also adds almost nothing from verse 89 itself, so it works mostly as a recap.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The question sets up the psalmist's hard times. Against that, the wrong answers 'He would have become a powerful king' and 'He would have sailed far away to sea' aren't believable as what would have happened without delight in God's law. The right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This closing card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse. It still cites Psalm 119:96, which card 12 already used.
findings.question: What should a story card cite when it carries only the 'story continues' line and tells no verse? Should it repeat the last verse, cite nothing, or something else?
